title: Ironhollow Rising Again
premise: Sable Quintana has spent his life in Ironhollow, a valley where magic cannot enter, serving as the king's food-taster and dosing himself with poisons to build immunity. When a dying courier presses a map into his hands—a map to the last dragon's hoard, which holds the ember that keeps magic alive beyond the valley—Sable becomes hunted by the crown, a zealot order, and the dragon's own dwindling kin. Leaving Ironhollow means surrendering the only place he was ever safe, and every ally he gains demands a truth he cannot afford to tell. In the end, Sable must choose between delivering the ember to the dying dragons or burning it to keep magic out of the world forever; he gives it back, accepting that survival without wonder is just another kind of death, and returns to Ironhollow changed, no longer invisible but no longer hiding.
about_author: Jude Kavanagh is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working kitchens before turning to fantasy, and whose fiction is obsessed with what people swallow—literally and otherwise. They live somewhere rainy with an opinionated cat and a growing collection of antique poison bottles.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Sable. A day in Ironhollow: Sable tastes the king's breakfast, survives a subtle arsenic attempt, and reflects on how he built his immunity dish by dish. Establishes the valley's magic-dead quiet and his deliberate invisibility. Emotional beat: the lonely comfort of routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Sable. A burned, half-mad courier collapses at Ironhollow's gate during a storm, muttering about embers and hoards. The guards want him gone; Sable, recognizing poison symptoms, takes him in secretly. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Dying Carry
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The courier dies of a slow toxin Sable can't counter, pressing a scorched map into Sable's hands and whispering 'the fire chooses its keeper.' Sable hides the map as the king's men arrive asking questions. Emotional beat: dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Questions in the Great Hall
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Royal investigator Dame Corvane interrogates the household about the stranger. Sable lies for the first time in his careful life and realizes how good he is at it—and how much he hates it. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Map That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Studying the map by candlelight, Sable finds marks matching stories his dead mother told: the Emberhoard, the last dragon Vaelithra, the source of all magic. Outside the valley, magic is real and fading. Emotional beat: awe colliding with terror.

chapters.title: Corvane's Patience
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. The investigator suspects Sable, not from evidence but instinct, and begins quietly dismantling his life—freezing his wages, questioning his neighbors. Introduces her conviction that magic must die completely. Emotional beat: cold menace.

chapters.title: The Only Door Out
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Smuggler Bren Oskar offers passage through the valley's one blind pass—for a price and a share of whatever Sable's carrying. Sable burns his savings, poisons his own records to fake his death, and walks out at dawn. Emotional beat: grief and exhilaration of leaving.

chapters.title: First Taste of Magic
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Beyond the valley border, magic floods him like a second heartbeat—terrifying, intoxicating. The party is ambushed by Ashcloaks, zealots who burn magic-users; Sable's immunity saves them when he breathes their smoke-poison unharmed. Emotional beat: the body as weapon.

chapters.title: Bren's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Bren. The smuggler reveals he knows what the map leads to—his sister died seeking the Emberhoard. He stays not for gold but for the chance she might be alive at the dragon's side. Emotional beat: loyalty built on shared wounds.

chapters.title: The City of Salt
chapters.summary: POV Sable. In the free city of Marrowgate, they seek a guide and find instead a bounty on Sable's head—Corvane's reach extends far. A young pickpocket, Wren, sells them out, then saves them when she learns who's hunting Sable. Emotional beat: trust extended cautiously.

chapters.title: Ashes and Zealots
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. Corvane allies with the Ashcloak High Father, revealing the crown's secret fear: if the ember dies, so does the old treaty protecting the realm. She believes destroying it cleanly is mercy. Emotional beat: antagonist made sympathetic.

chapters.title: Wren's Truth
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The girl confesses she was paid by both sides and begs to come along; Sable refuses, then catches her following anyway. On the road she reveals she can hear the mountains humming—she's magic-touched, exactly what the Ashcloaks hunt. Emotional beat: found family forming under threat.

chapters.title: The Poisoned Road
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Ambushed with tainted water, Bren falls deathly ill; Sable must synthesize an antidote from memory and roadside plants while Wren holds off pursuers. He saves Bren but exhausts his immunity reserves. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Vaelithra's Shadow
chapters.summary: POV Sable. They reach the Ashen Peaks and find a valley of bones—dragons who came to die beside their queen. Vaelithra appears, vast and guttering, and reads Sable's mind: the map chose him because his mother was the last Keeper. Emotional beat: inheritance he never asked for.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Blood
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Vaelithra shows him visions: his mother fled Ironhollow pregnant, trading magic for safety, and the map was her insurance. The ember can reignite dragonkind—or be destroyed forever. Sable rages at being conscripted by blood. Emotional beat: fury at destiny.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hoard
chapters.summary: POV Bren. Corvane's forces arrive, guided by a tracker Bren unknowingly led here; worse, Wren trades herself to the Ashcloaks to buy the others time. Bren's guilt fractures the group. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: The Choice of Embers
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At the hoard's heart, Sable holds the ember as Corvane offers a deal: destroy it and go home pardoned, or die with the dragons. He sees the war it could reignite—and the slow extinction refusing guarantees. Emotional beat: the fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The Ashcloaks attack the hoard; Vaelithra rises for one last fight, buying Sable time to decide. Wren escapes her captors in the chaos, and Bren returns despite everything. Sable understands: the ember isn't power, it's a life. Emotional beat: clarity through fire.

chapters.title: What Sable Swallowed
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Climax: rather than destroy or hoard the ember, Sable does what a taster does—he takes it into himself, becoming the living vessel, sharing it with Vaelithra and the gathered bones. Magic doesn't reignite as war; it rekindles as renewal. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Cost Paid
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. Witnessing the rebirth, Corvane breaks—her zealotry was grief for a magic-ruined childhood. She withdraws the bounty and turns on the High Father, though it costs her everything. Emotional beat: justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable returns to Ironhollow carrying magic inside him for the first time—and must face the king, the court, and the truth of what he is. Instead of execution, the valley's elders offer a new role: warden of the border between worlds. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: Rising Again
chapters.summary: POV Sable, epilogue. One year later: dragons wheel over distant peaks, Wren trains as the first valley-born mage, Bren sails new routes. Sable tastes the king's food still—but now he chooses each morning whether to stay visible. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
